fbs_sms.license: No explicit SPDX license; public research release requests source attribution and CCS2020 citation.
fbs_sms.citation: Zhang et al. (2020), Lies in the Air: Characterizing Fake-base-station Spam Ecosystem in China, doi:10.1145/3372297.3417257
fbs_sms.semantics: Real de-identified fake-base-station SMS. AD:* means advertising spam; FR:* means fraud. IL:* and Other are excluded because they do not define the requested three-class target.
fbs_sms.limitations: Spam reflects unsolicited fake-base-station delivery, which text alone cannot always establish. Word segmentation and anonymization are source preprocessing artifacts.

mudou_sms.license: No license is specified in this public mirror. Upstream provenance and redistribution/commercial rights are unresolved; local research prototype only.
mudou_sms.semantics: Chinese SMS: 0 normal, 1 spam. Only original training-file normal rows enter three-class training; spam rows cannot be reliably divided into fraud versus advertising and are excluded. Original test file is reserved for binary external evaluation only.
mudou_sms.limitations: Mirror rather than original data collector. Some normal-labelled rows contain marketing, so class labels reflect source annotation, not consent inferred from wording.

telecom_fraud_5.license: Repository GPL-3.0 plus README explicitly restricts dataset to university/research-institution scientific research and prohibits commercial use.
telecom_fraud_5.semantics: label00 normal ->0; label01 government impersonation, label02 loans, label03 customer-service impersonation, label04 acquaintance impersonation ->2.
telecom_fraud_5.limitations: Mixed normal SMS and case-derived/generated fraud messages or phone dialogue; these are not all independently captured real SMS. Do not interpret combined test performance as real-SMS-only deployment accuracy.

smishing_imc2025.citation: Agarwal et al. (2025), Fishing for Smishing: Understanding SMS Phishing Infrastructure and Strategies by Mining Public User Reports, doi:10.1145/3730567.3764431
smishing_imc2025.semantics: Preserve Chinese-language public reports as unlabelled external diagnostics. scam_type is a topical field and is NOT a validated normal/spam/scam label.
smishing_imc2025.limitations: Chinese subset includes anti-fraud notices, genuine-looking appointments, truncated messages, and ambiguous wrong-number contacts. All-scam mapping would corrupt the benchmark. No formal accuracy metric is justified without independent label review.

nus_sms.license: Public research release requests paper attribution; no explicit SPDX license in repository.
nus_sms.citation: Chen and Kan (2013), Creating a Live, Public Short Message Service Corpus: The NUS SMS Corpus, Language Resources and Evaluation 47(2).
nus_sms.semantics: Volunteer personal SMS in Simplified and genuine Traditional Chinese; no scam/spam classification labels. Retained archive only, not assigned guessed ground truth.

fgrc_scd.license: MIT stated in dataset card; underlying source-case terms still apply
fgrc_scd.semantics: Generated SMS from CCF23-EVAL task6 cases; 无风险->normal0, nine named risk categories->scam2. Actual case IDs preserved and kept within one split.
fgrc_scd.limitations: Generated message-form data, not an independent real-SMS corpus. Existing Telecom source lacks case IDs, so cross-source case identity can only be screened using text similarity and cannot be guaranteed completely.
